title: Chapter 2: Walking the Beaten Path Together 4
content: "Well then, from here on out..."
I swallowed the bread and bacon I had bought from the villagers before continuing.
Since this was a day trip, I hadn't prepared any camping gear, so we were having breakfast sitting on the ground.
Fortunately, the grassland was soft, so it wasn't uncomfortable.
"Since there's nothing else to do, I think I'll ask the villagers about the sightings."
Erika, sitting on the ground and simply drinking from her water bottle, looked so dignified that it dazzled me even in the morning light.

"I considered following the carriage to the town as a form of escort, but from their perspective, having a rank 1 adventurer they don't know following them would probably be more concerning, so I decided against it."

If it were against a Bonbo, I could at least leave the luggage behind and escape, but with humans, it wouldn't be that simple. The villagers would be much more worried about being followed by outsiders like us.
"However, since we've dealt with the swarm of Bonbos, I think the villagers will trust that the monsters have been subjugated in a day or two."
While that wouldn't count as quest completion, at least the village would likely stop sending requests to the guild.
Eventually, more monsters would probably appear, but that was a different story.
Though they might not trust us, I believed the problem would resolve itself with time.
The village was large when including the fields, but the inhabited area was quite small.
With a population of around two hundred, it was considered large for a farming village, but it didn't take long to hear from those who had actually witnessed the monsters.
It seemed that only a few designated individuals were sent to the town to sell crops, and the number of people who had actually seen the monsters was surprisingly low.
As the sun passed its zenith, I finished hearing the last witness's account and thanked them, walking alongside Erika toward the tool shed.

We were collecting testimonies about the monster sightings from the villagers. The main reason was that we had nothing else to do, but I also felt a sense of discomfort from when I had greeted everyone while distributing meat yesterday.
"What do you think about the witnesses' stories?"
That discomfort might have been valid; I thought as I asked Erika.
"What do you mean by that?"
Erika responded to my vague question with a question of her own.
"Were there any suspicious aspects?"
As I asked, Erika murmured, "Suspicious aspects?" and pondered for a moment.
"If I had to say, I felt they were observing closely. That caught my attention."
Yes, that was it. Seeing me nod, Erika continued.
"The villagers' accounts of being attacked by the monsters were all unmistakably clear that they were attacked by Bonbos. The details were so precise that it was as if they had known beforehand."
Erika stopped and looked at me.
"I had thought that villagers would have at least some knowledge of monster characteristics, but is that not the case?"
I shook my head in response to Erika's question.
"Normally, unless they're adventurers, they wouldn't know. Especially if they were being attacked, it's rare for someone to remember and observe the details."

When requests like this are made to the Adventurer Guild, they usually stem from vague sightings of the monsters. For example, if there's a monkey-like monster in that area, they might speculate on the fur color.

But this time, it was explicitly stated that it was a Bonbo, and furthermore, the witnesses' accounts were unusually detailed. It was as if they had coordinated beforehand, with similar content in their testimonies.
I scratched the back of my neck.
Something feels off.
As I was thinking that, I noticed small footsteps approaching from behind.
Turning around, I saw a little girl holding a small wooden figurine, staring intently at Erika and me.
The little girl spoke.
"Are you an adventurer, big sister?"
Erika and I exchanged glances in surprise.
Erika, who met my gaze, quickly shook off her momentary confusion and stepped forward gracefully in front of the little girl.
With a soft smile, Erika knelt down to meet the girl's eyes.
"Yes, that's right. We are adventurers."
The little girl glanced at both our faces, then showed a moment of contemplation before her eyes filled with serious determination.
"I want to ask the adventurers for a favor."
Erika did not belittle the little girl's words or her seriousness.
"Can you tell us what kind of favor it is?"
The little girl seemed to recall something, biting her lip for a moment before saying,
"Please defeat the monster that hurt my daddy."
"I understand."
Erika answered immediately.
Hmm, that's cool.
"But I'm sorry, but the monster that probably hurt your father has already been defeated. I went a bit overboard, so there’s no evidence left."
The little girl shook her head.
"No, it’s not that. It wasn’t a little monkey monster."
So, the Bonbo is being referred to as a little monkey. I didn't take the girl's statement as just a child's words.
And I felt the discomfort I had been sensing settle into clarity.
I see, the village chief is lying.
Is this... a common pattern?
"I'm sorry, but I’d like to hear your father's story. Can you guide me to him?"
I tried to speak as gently as possible, but for some reason, the little girl trembled and looked scared, and Erika shot me a glare.
Why?
The little girl's father was one of those tasked with transporting the village's crops to the town. By the way, he was currently out of that role due to his injuries.
And I had been told by others in the same role that he was not present.
In other words, it was being hidden by the entire village.
At first, the little girl's father tried to feign ignorance.
He lied that his injuries were from farming and even apologized for his daughter saying something strange.
But when I revealed what I roughly understood, Erika reproached him for disregarding his daughter's feelings, who was worried about him and wanted to take revenge on the monster.
Eventually, the little girl started crying, and he finally relented.
After leaving the little girl's house, I let out a sigh. Well, it was a common occurrence.
Especially in villages near towns with guilds like this farming village.
Now, what should we do next? Just as I was pondering that...
I spotted a broken-covered cart racing toward the village at full speed.
It wasn't a very large village.
The commotion quickly spread, and by the time the cart reached the village entrance, a large crowd of villagers had gathered.
Erika and I stood a little distance away, wondering what was happening.
"Village chief, it's bad! That thing has appeared!"
As the coachman stopped the cart, he shouted upon spotting the village chief.
For a brief moment, the chief glanced our way, but the coachman, either panicking or too focused on the situation, continued to shout.
"That thing intends to come to this village! We need to escape quickly!"
"What!?"
The village chief shouted in surprise.
That thing is coming; the words caused the surrounding villagers to start murmuring anxiously.
The kind of foolishness that delays decision-making due to the unique anxiety of those unaccustomed to chaos. It quickly turned into a panic with the roar of the monster heard from afar.
The time spent hesitating only led to regret and panic.
The villagers all fled the scene at once.
The village chief raised his voice, trying to restore some order, but it was already too difficult.
The coachman, in a state that was the easiest to escape, remained there, likely because the villagers were in the way. He looked like he would bolt the moment he had a clear path.
Just then, a woman emerged from the cart, gasping for breath.
Instead of stepping down, she seemed to slide down to the ground, leaning against the cart as she spoke to the village chief.
"I will hold off the monster, so please evacuate quickly."
I couldn't help but frown at the sight of the blonde woman.
A sister, a member of the church.
Our eyes met.
She pressed a bloodied side while smiling and said,
"You should evacuate quickly as well."
I wanted to avoid getting involved with church members if possible.
To me, they were the ones who had taken away Erika Solnzali's bright future.
In this farce, there was nothing good that could come from getting involved.
Ah—but you...
You say this.
"Are you joking?"
Because you are Erika Solnzali.
I looked at Erika's profile, feeling my heart race at how close we were.
What am I saying? The question was clearly visible on my face.
Of course, it was directed at the sister.

Church sisters are typically skilled in magic, having trained day and night in the divine arts as part of their duties, often surpassing ordinary adventurers in magical prowess. According to the church's philosophy, while their offensive magic may be less refined, they still possess the capability of a typical rank 5 adventurer.

The village chief, who knew I was a rank 1 adventurer, looked at me as if doubting my sanity. The sister, on the other hand, probably couldn't understand Erika's reaction, as she had just told us to run, despite appearing to be a regular person with a sword at her side.
Still, what kind of monster could injure a young church sister? I pondered while listening to the distant roar of the monster.
"Village chief, what exactly has been appearing around the village?"
I decided to ask someone who seemed to know.
"What are you talking about?"
Despite having heard the coachman mention that thing right in front of him, he tried to feign ignorance.
Well, whatever. I'll find out soon enough. Ignoring the village chief, I approached the sister.
The sister, confused by the exchange between the village chief and me, couldn’t hide her bewilderment but quickly regained her serious demeanor.
"This is not the time for idle chatter. You must escape immediately. I will buy you time."
"Erika."
"Yes."
Erika crouched in front of the sister, ignoring her surprise, and suddenly tore a part of her habit. The black robe was darkened with blood.
The sister froze in shock.
"Your broken rib is protruding from your abdomen."
"Ugh."
Whether she hadn't known her condition or had chosen not to check, the sister groaned as she realized the details of her injury.
"At this rate, no matter what you face, you will die without even fighting."
"Sister, what about healing magic?"
"I have a little healing magic, but... I'm not very good at it."
The sister managed to look embarrassed while still in pain.
It must be embarrassing for her to admit that she's not good at something she was taught as a priority in the church.
"I see. Well, you can use a bit of it yourself. We will go subjugate that 'thing' that is coming."
"What are you saying? That thing is a monster..."
The sister seemed about to reveal the identity of the monster I wanted to know, but it became unnecessary as I caught sight of it.
"A Golden Ogre."
As I extended my gaze to confirm the opponent, the sister let out a soft "Ah."
It was more of a lamentation towards us for not trying to escape than a voice of agreement.
I ignored that.
"I can't just abandon a little girl who cares for her father."
That can't be the case. I thought, but if Erika seemed hesitant to fight, I would consider other options and spoke in a confirming tone.
"Oh? Is that a provocation?"
Erika's voice seemed to hold gratitude rather than anger.
So I exaggeratedly shrugged my shoulders and feigned nonchalance.
"Of course not. I'm just relieved to know the leading actress has no complaints about her co-star."
The script might be a bit cheap, I thought as I laughed at Erika, and I steeled myself.
"Hey, you."
I called out to the coachman, who looked utterly inconvenienced by our presence, unable to escape.
"Please tell the villagers who fled outside the village not to run too far."
"What are you talking about?"
That was the village chief. I ignored him and nodded at Erika.
For some reason, it felt like we understood each other with just that.
Erika nodded back at me, then slipped her hand under the sister's arm, ignoring the sister's bewildered protests, and helped her sit against a nearby fence.
It must have taken all her strength just to stand up from the cart, and once seated in such a situation, getting back up would be quite difficult.
I deliberately spoke to the village chief.
"This isn't what you wanted, but I will subjugate that thing. After all, I've accepted a request from a little girl who cares for her father."
"Please don't blame me. I will make sure to consult properly before accepting requests in the future."
What did the village chief see when he looked at us?
A rank 1 adventurer who doesn't even know his own abilities?
Or perhaps two young people who have lost their minds?
Well, he probably couldn't even see Erika's true strength. Whatever he thought, it didn't matter much. Magic power flowed through my body.
I focused my strength into my legs.
"Sister, please wait a moment. I will take care of this quickly."
At Erika's words, we took off running.
The Golden Ogre.
A monster with a straightforward name that fits its nature. Just as its name suggests, it is an ogre with golden skin.
Though it has a simple name, it is a troublesome monster.
Magic is less effective against it, and its tough skin, combined with the power of its massive attacks, means that if you take a hit unguarded, you could easily die.
For a typical adventurer, taking it down safely alone is said to require at least rank 7, depending on their type.
Unless one is exceptionally skilled or exceptionally reckless, it's not something one would consider tackling solo.
It's not a matter of ability; it's a matter of safety. Adventurers' bodies are their capital. It's normal for them to want to avoid injuries as much as possible.
The Golden Ogre roared, having noticed us.
Even though it was still far away, the roar filled with magic power made my body tremble.
"Three simultaneous roars are indeed impressive."
Erika frowned at the roars of the three Golden Ogres.
She must have imagined what would happen when they reached the village.
"Which one should we take down first?"
Erika showed no signs of fear at the three Golden Ogres and asked which one we should deal with first, looking quite cool.
"We'll start with the one on the right. We can't let them enter the village, so we need to diminish their mobility first."
The Golden Ogre is a rare type of monster in this area, but it's relatively common in the Faltarl Kingdom. My master often had me hunt them.
Though I had never faced three at once before.
Upon hearing my words, magic power swelled around Erika.
"First, we'll use a distraction."
The distance between us was about a hundred feet. Though Erika called it a distraction, I was taken aback by the scale of it.
Dozens of fire arrows floated around Erika.
Fire arrows are a well-known spell, but typically, it's one shot at a time.

I had known many who could shoot fire arrows in succession, but this was the first time I had seen someone unleash a large number of them simultaneously. As golden magic power shimmered, the fire arrows were released.
This power cannot simply be called a distraction.
I thought as I watched the Golden Ogre hurriedly shield its head with its arms in defense against the incoming fire arrows.
The fire arrows rained down on the Golden Ogre, causing numerous small explosions around it.
This was certainly not a sight one would see for a mere distraction, and I quickly enhanced my body. The soft earth of the farm road erupted.
"Fast!"
Erika's faint murmur already felt distant.
By the time Erika murmured, I was already behind the Golden Ogre, which was still in a defensive stance, crouched low. I slashed at its unguarded ankles as I ran past.
The Golden Ogre let out a pained groan.
The Golden Ogre swung its arms wildly, but by that time, I had already created some distance. A moment later, Erika arrived next to me.
"I couldn't keep up."
She sounded somewhat dissatisfied for some reason.
"Isn't it the lady's etiquette to let the man take the lead?"
"Right now, I'm an adventurer."
I felt like that conversation about etiquette had also been during our time as adventurers, but I didn't voice it. I wasn't that foolish.
Moreover, the Golden Ogre was now glaring at us with eyes filled with hatred. We were locked in a stare at close range, just a few feet away, where we could attack.
According to my master, the one who averts their gaze loses at this distance.
The three Golden Ogres charged at us, moving with a speed approaching that of rank 2 or 3 adventurers. Despite having its ankle cut, it was still moving well, but it was slow.
Before I could move, Erika's magic power indicated that she trusted me.
As I had said earlier, I dashed toward the rightmost Golden Ogre while Erika directed her magic toward the other two.
As I dodged the massive fist swung down by the rightmost Golden Ogre, I used its arm as a springboard to leap up.
Then, I maximized my body enhancement and extended it to my sword as well.
It was one of the few practical spells I could use, as I wasn't very good with magic.
The effect was that my sword became sturdier, and that was all.
By the way, it has no name, because I'm the only one who uses it. At least, I don't know anyone else who does.

My master said that if I were going to use such a ridiculous spell, I might as well use a sturdy sword, and if I could do something so skillful, I should polish other magic instead. But as the second son of a poor viscount family, this spell was incredibly useful. Why?
Because even if I tried to cut the thick neck of the Golden Ogre, which would normally chip the blade, it wouldn't chip at all.
As the Golden Ogre's head separated from its body, the body rapidly changed. The golden skin color faded quickly to a light gray, and the biological softness disappeared.
As I landed and turned around, the body collapsed with a loud crash.

When a monster dies, it leaves behind a magic stone known as a core, and its body transforms into magic stone fragments, which are pale gray crystals. Sometimes parts of the body remain, but this time there were none. No luck.
Two left!
With that thought, I focused even more strength into my limbs when I caught sight of something that left me momentarily dumbfounded.

A fireball, a commonly used spell for distractions, simple and easy to use, with adjustable power, and due to its ease of construction, some people say that if you have fire magic, this is all you need.
The fireball.
At that moment, two fireballs struck the faces of the remaining two Golden Ogres.
The Golden Ogre's golden skin is famous for being resistant to magic.
If the power isn't sufficient, it's not uncommon for it to be deflected.
In fact, the fire arrows Erika had used earlier managed to hold them back, but they hadn't inflicted any real damage on the Golden Ogre, which had focused on defense.
The power of magic is proportional to the amount of magic power infused and the complexity of the magic circle constructed within the body.
Quickly cast spells have simple magic circles, making it difficult to infuse magic power.
Generally, if one tries to use a powerful spell, it takes time to activate because a more complex magic circle, which allows for greater magic power infusion, needs to be constructed.
However, that doesn't mean that simple magic circles can't have magic power infused into them.
It simply means they are inefficient.
When that inefficiency is pushed to its limits, this is what happens.
It's unreasonable.
I thought as I watched the Golden Ogre recoil after taking a fireball to the face.
One was barely alive, but the other’s head was half-destroyed.
I couldn't even imagine how much absurd magic power was needed to produce such force with a fireball. My moment of forgetfulness was quickly dispelled by the roar of the Golden Ogre.
The Golden Ogre, with its head half-destroyed, let out a roar that sounded like a death cry.
Erika was not careless.
That’s why her focus was already directed toward the other Golden Ogre.
The roar that struck it was one of desperation, the most powerful sound it could muster in its final moments.
As its body began to crystallize, the roar momentarily robbed Erika of her freedom.
Letting out a terribly human-like battle cry, the remaining Golden Ogre raised both its hands.
Its skin torn by the fireball, its face burned and distorted, flesh ripped open to reveal bone, Erika steeled herself for the impact.
There was no way I could allow that.
Before I knew it, I had positioned myself between Erika and the Golden Ogre.
No, it was only natural to do so, but my thoughts hadn't caught up with my actions.
The battle cry that erupted from my throat, the magic power surging through my entire body, everything was leaving my thoughts behind.
